scale: showcase (2,000 jobs, Anthropic, batch tier, claude-sonnet-5)
notes: 2,000/2,000 SLAs met, 2 sync fallbacks, 49.9% captured, 19m20s end to end including polling, on claude-sonnet-5 against a 12h deadline.

The work is real: five public-domain novels from Project Gutenberg (War and Peace, Les Miserables, Don Quixote, Anna Karenina, Middlemarch) cut into 2,000 passages of roughly 1,300 tokens, one three-sentence summarisation per passage. Long novels on purpose — 2,000 passages of that size needs about 10.4M characters and five average novels hold roughly a third of it.

Two jobs missed the batch tier and were rescued synchronously at list, which is why capture reads 49.9% rather than the structural 50.0%: $0.006139 left on the table. Both rescued jobs still met the deadline, so the SLA is 2,000/2,000 with 2 fell back. The cause was not the venue: both errored with invalid_request_error, "credit balance is too low" (request ids workerreq_013qCbZ7LXVvdSGTDfP35LpL and workerreq_012NbUh8dANVyvrp1dXYLuPx). The account ran short two requests from the end of its own batch. Re-run unchanged after topping up as 2026-09-10-sonnet-showcase-2, which captured 50.0% with zero fallbacks — so the 49.9% here is a billing state on our side, not a tier behaviour.

The quote under-read the bill. Its input estimate is characters/4, which priced 2,853,653 input tokens against an actual 3,976,002 — 39.3% low on 19th-century prose, whose long words and heavy punctuation tokenise worse than the ratio assumes. Quoted list was $9.7073; settled list was $11.9364, which cleared the $12.00 hard cap by $0.0636. The cap gate is priced off the quote, so on this corpus it guarded a number 19% below the one that arrived. A cap is only as good as the estimator underneath it.

Output ran to the ceiling rather than under it: 199.2 tokens mean against a 200-token max_tokens, min 147. A three-sentence summary of 1,300 tokens of Tolstoy uses the whole allowance, so unlike the mechanics proofs there is almost no gap here between pricing a ceiling and pricing an answer.
